questions.stem: What feature must a monomer have in order to undergo addition polymerisation?

options.text: It must contain a C=C double bond
It must be a saturated hydrocarbon

questions.explanation: Addition polymerisation requires monomers with a C=C double bond. During the reaction, the double bond opens up and monomers join end-to-end to form a long chain. Only one product (the polymer) is formed, with no small molecule released.

questions.stem: Which environmental problem is most associated with addition polymers?

options.text: They release toxic gases at room temperature
They are non-biodegradable and persist in the environment
They dissolve in water and poison fish
They react with oxygen in the air causing smog

questions.explanation: Addition polymers like poly(ethene) and PVC are non-biodegradable because they have no functional groups that natural enzymes can break down. They only have strong C-C single bonds in the chain. This means they persist in landfill and the environment for hundreds of years, causing pollution.
